reason: Reproduced on cards.edit-limit-modal: Esc closes the dialog and focus lands on the More button, which opened the menu. The Edit limit menu item is gone: the menu closes when the item is activated, and the item is no longer in the DOM, so there is nothing to return to. More has no visible focus ring afterwards; that is a focus-visible matter, not this finding's claim.
criterionAnalysis: 2.4.3 Focus Order: after Esc, focus moves to the More button that launched the menu and then the dialog, which is the control the user came from, so the sequence keeps its meaning. The menu item the check expected no longer exists after activation. 3.2.1 On Focus: no context change on focus. 2.4.7 Focus Visible: More shows no focus indicator after the return, but that is a separate measured family on a different element and is not what this finding claims. No A or AA criterion fails for the focus return itself.

reason: On cards.edit-limit-modal the title Edit card limits is a plain span (19px/400) with no heading role, and the dialog contains no heading at all; the ax node is ignored with no role (probe-3a555673ada0). The Change Card Nickname modal on cards.edit-nickname uses an H2, so only the edit-limit modal fails 1.3.1. Impact is minor: the title is still the first text in the dialog.

The trash icon button beside Temporary limit change scheduled has no accessible name (probe-3a9855f74732: button ""), no aria-describedby and no visible tooltip on focus. It removes the scheduled limit change and no other control in the dialog does the same, so 4.1.2 fails and a screen-reader user cannot tell what it does. It is not a form control or the dialog's primary action, so it stays medium.

On both states the Limit type combobox carries autocomplete="garbage", an invalid token used to switch off browser autofill. The field picks Weekly or Monthly and collects nothing about the user, and the tree exposes it correctly as combobox "Limit type" (probe-38baabfed568, probe-1973455bfd35).
criterionAnalysis: 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose only covers fields that collect information about the user; Limit type is a limit period selector, so it does not apply, and an unrecognised token breaks nothing for assistive technology. 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value: the field has a name, a role and its expanded and haspopup states in the tree. 4.1.1 Parsing is removed from WCAG 2.2. No A or AA criterion fails.
